slides.title: Where does the **cache** sit between your app and DB?
**Cache-aside** (lazy loading)
flow: 💾 App stores it in cache with a TTL

slides.title: On write, **delete**, don't update
slides.text: Updating can leave a stale value if two writers race. Deleting lets the next read refill it.
slides.code:
read:  GET → miss → SELECT → SET EX 300
write: UPDATE db → DEL key

slides.title: **Read-through**

cols.title: 🙋 Cache-aside
cols.text: App loads the DB on a miss.

cols.title: 🧰 Read-through
cols.text: The cache layer loads the DB. App only talks to cache.

slides.text: Redis does not load your DB by itself. You need a library or layer.

slides.title: **Write-through**
slides.text: Always consistent. Slower writes. May cache data nobody reads.

slides.title: **Write-back** (write-behind)
flow: ⏳ Flushed to DB later, in batches
slides.text: Super fast writes. If the cache dies before the flush, you lose data.

slides.title: Say this in 1 line
slides.text: **Cache-aside**: check cache, load DB on miss, **delete the key on write**. **Write-through** is consistent but slower, **write-back** is fastest but can **lose data**. Default to cache-aside with a TTL.
